# task\-w07a\-binding\-store — W07a: worker binding store, generation and lifecycle
status: todo  priority: 2  scope: scope-mcp
readiness: not_eligible  reason: status_todo

Implement the plugin's binding store and lifecycle: an explicit binding command in the worker or coordinator context taking a registered project key, a worker worktree and a stable Waystation actor; and a stored binding carrying binding ID and generation, local runtime and profile identity, verified host\-supplied durable session or lineage identity, actual delegated\-worker identity when needed, registration key and revision with pinned route and root, absolute canonical caller worktree and actor, and creation and update metadata with active or retired state\. Validation refuses to infer session identity from model text, task titles, agent names or the active UI tab; a Hermes task identifier is never a Waystation task ID; separate delegated workers require distinct bindings whenever their execution context differs, and binding or dispatch is refused with an actionable diagnostic when the host cannot distinguish them reliably\. A project, worktree or actor change requires an explicit rebind with no in\-flight calls or active claims on the old binding, while a verified same worker reattaching after restart is a resume rather than a rebind\.

## Acceptance
- Two workers on one project connection hold distinct bindings, and two projects with identical task and actor names resolve to their own project\.
- A verified resume keeps the same binding, while a project, worktree or actor change without an explicit rebind is refused, including while in\-flight calls or active claims reference the old binding\.
- Identical actor or task names in different projects are valid, while a second active binding for the same actor inside one project is refused\.
- An unverifiable session identity, such as a delegated worker or a compressed session without lineage, refuses binding with an actionable diagnostic instead of guessing\.
